newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index ends sharply up as interims near.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends sharply up as interims near.

text.p: Shenzhen B shares surged to a sharply higher close on Friday, on an extended rebound powered by bargain hunting in under-valued issues expected to post strong interim results, analysts said.

The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index leapt 6.77 points or 5.39 percent to 132.36 on turnover of HK$87.8 million against Thursday's HK$95 million. The rebound began on Thursday after the index ended Wednesday at a 1997 low of 120.44 points.
The A share index roared up 17.88 points or 4.70 percent to 398.22 on turnover of 5.6 billion yuan, compared with Thursday's 4.4 billion.
"Both the A and B share markets are staging strong technical rebounds after the recent plunges gave them no room to fall any further," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.

"Many investors picked relatively cheap shares in companies expected to post strong interim results, and that pushed up the indices," the analyst said. Shenzhen-listed firms must publish their 1997 first-half results by August 30.
Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd, a market heavyweight, was among the heaviest B share gainers and surged to its 10 percent limit-up at HK$2.93.
Recently-listed Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd was the most heavily traded on volume of 3.6 million shares, rising HK$0.54 to HK$7.45.
"These shares are expected to have fared nicely in the first half," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Analysts had mixed views on where the indices would go next week.
"I think the markets will ease on Monday as there is no good news to support them," an analyst at PBI Securities (HK) said.
But the Guotai analyst said: "The markets should plough higher on follow-up buying."
